Q: Privileges for user-defined functions in join predicates A:

The behavior appears to be self-contradictory. If you are not allowed to run f() then you should not be allowed to run it in any circumstances, not even in views. Imagine the case when you have a really costly function and you don't want it to be executed by anyone else than a superadmin. What if someone is allowed to use views? In that case the user may be able to run that function if it's in the view. So a lower-level user could cause huge server load at will, even if not allowed.

Another problematic scenario is when the function does some "magic" work, something really important not to be shared with just anyone who creates views. This behavior could leak the results.

So I would say this is inconsistent and insecure.

So if you don't want your users to execute f(), then, instead of creating a view that executes it, you are better off by:

  • creating a table, let's call it t_f where the result of f() is stored
  • have a stored procedure which runs f(), processes the results and stores them in t_f, possibly cleaning t_f at the start, depending on what your intention is
  • have a user allowed to run this stored procedure
  • execute this stored procedure on behalf of the user who is allowed to do it periodically, or schedule it

Q: How to abort a git rebase from inside vim during interactive editing A:

Yet another hack: have the first action of your rebase instructions be:

exec git rebase --abort  # <- type this line
pick ...

Q: How to create a multi-variable "ts" object in R? A:

I tend to do things along the lines

x = read.table(text = '
Year Grocery_Stores Liquor
Feb-11 1953.8 216.8
Mar-11 2108.1 240.5
Apr-11 2062.3 244.4
May-11 2034.8 232.1
Jun-11 1988.6 223.6
Jul-11 2085.9 239.0
', header = TRUE)

local({
  
  tmstmp = 
    sprintf(fmt = '01-%s', x$Year) |> 
    as.Date(format='%d-%b-%y') |> 
    min() |> 
    as.POSIXlt() |> 
    with.default(c(year + 1900, mon + 1))
  
  x |>
    subset(select=-Year) |> 
    ts(start=tmstmp, frequency=12L)
  
})

Time Series:
Start = 1 
End = 6 
Frequency = 12 
  Grocery_Stores Liquor
1         1953.8  216.8
2         2108.1  240.5
3         2062.3  244.4
4         2034.8  232.1
5         1988.6  223.6
6         2085.9  239.0

(Note not all of those coercions are needed, but they might be informative.)
